title: Security Release Rollforward Authorization Workflow and Evidence Pack
content:
Purpose:
This working runbook describes the authorization workflow and minimum evidence required to approve a release rollforward (gradual re-enablement or scale-up after a blocked release) and to approve short-term security exceptions during a release window. It focuses on items that tie directly into RBAC v2 changes, audit log schema verification, evidence export automation, and SIEM onboarding.

Intended audience:
- Security reviewers and approvers
- Release engineers and oncall SREs
- Product owners coordinating rollouts
- Solutions / Professional Services when private deployments are affected

High-level goals:
1) Provide a compact checklist for release authorities to approve a rollforward safely.
2) Ensure all required audit/evidence artifacts are generated automatically where possible.
3) Standardize the exception approval envelope to reduce ad-hoc signoffs.
4) Validate SIEM export and audit schema compatibility before re-enabling traffic.

Scope / When to use this doc:
- Release rollforward after a deployment has been paused due to security/observability concerns.
- Short-term exceptions to RBAC or network policy during an urgent release (timeboxed, with compensating controls).
- Onboarding a release path into SIEM export for new model/runtime variants.

Roles & approvers (minimum):
- Release Lead (RL): owns deployment orchestration and rollout plan.
- Security Reviewer (SR): senior security engineer who vets RBAC/audit changes.
- Observability Lead (OL): validates SIEM exports, dashboards, and alerting coverage.
- SRE Oncall (SRE): ensures infra readiness and rollback paths are available.
- Privacy/Compliance (PC): for private deployments or regulated customers.

Rollforward authorization checklist (gated items — all must be signed or documented):
1) RBAC v2 sanity check
   - Confirm new roles/role-bindings scoped to least privilege. List of changed bindings attached.
   - Service account changes: verify ephemeral tokens and expiry policies applied.
   - Any new cluster-admin grants require SR + PC signoff.
2) Audit log schema verification
   - Verify events emitted include required fields: timestamp, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, outcome, k8s_namespace (if applicable), model_variant.
   - Confirm log sample for the release contains >= 10 representative events for each sensitive action type (auth grant, secret access, model load, config-change).
3) SIEM export & parsing
   - Ensure SIEM pipeline ingests audit events with expected field mapping (index name, evt_type, severity, host, env).
   - Run the ingestion smoke test and show results for one hour of simulated traffic or replayed logs.
4) Evidence automation artifacts present
   - Evidence bucket/path created (S3 or internal object store) with write-once permissions.
   - Automated collection jobs (CI/CD post-hook or sidecar) produce: deployment manifest, RBAC diff, audit sample, helm/terraform plan output, and canary metrics snapshot.
5) Canary & metrics gating
   - Define canary window, success criteria (latency, error budget, anomaly rate), and rollback thresholds.
   - Metrics dashboard link and alert runbook attached.
6) Emergency exception containment plan
   - If an exception is needed (e.g., elevated role for a short window), list compensating controls: timeboxed duration, elevated role audit stream flagged, mandatory approver, and automated revocation job.
7) Final sign-offs
   - Required: RL, SR, OL, SRE. Optional: PC if private/regulatory scope.

Minimum evidence package (automated-first):
- RBAC-diff.txt (git diff or terraform plan) — sample of changed bindings (attach full diff).
- audit-sample.ndjson — 10–50 sample events covering critical actions.
- siem-ingest-check.log — output of SIEM smoke test (timestamped).
- canary-snapshot.json — metrics snapshot at start and end of canary (latency P50/P95, errors, token-count).
- deployment-manifest.yaml — exact manifests applied.
- revocation-proof.txt — confirmation baseline showing no lingering elevated credentials after revocation job runs.

Evidence automation notes / how to produce items quickly:
- RBAC diffs: CI job `rbac-diff` runs `terraform plan -out=plan && terraform show -json plan | jq .` and writes plan JSON to evidence bucket.
- Audit samples: use `audit-replay` tool to collect last-n events filtered by request_id range; write NDJSON to evidence path.
- SIEM test: `siem-smoke --replay evidence/audit-sample.ndjson --verify` returns structured status. Save output file.
- Canary snapshots: `canary-export --from $(date -d '10 minutes ago' +%s) --to $(date +%s) --metrics latency,error_rate`
- Revocation proof: automated job `elevated-revoke-check` queries IAM and returns a signed timestamped assertion.

RBAC v2 specific checks (short reference):
- Role naming convention: team:action:resource (example: infra:attach-kv:dedicated-pool).
- Ensure each role has an owning team tag and a POC.
- Verify use of ephemeral creds for operator-run CLI flows. Long-lived tokens must be justified and timeboxed.
- Cross-account or cross-tenant grants must include a recorded business justification in the evidence pack.

Audit log schema - minimum fields and formats (enforce in pipeline):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string
- event_id / request_id: UUID
- principal_id: string (user/service account)
- principal_type: one of [user, service, job, system]
- action: verb (e.g., grant, revoke, load_model, infer, config_update)
- resource_type: e.g., model, endpoint, secret, cluster
- resource_id: string identifier
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- src_ip: IPv4/IPv6 or empty
- user_agent: optional string
- trace_id: optional for distributed tracing
- meta: freeform string (for legacy fields)

SIEM export mapping recommendations:
- index: security-audit-{env}-{yyyy.MM.dd}
- doc_type: audit_event
- fields to map: [timestamp, severity, evt_type, principal_id, resource_type, action, outcome, request_id, trace_id, env, host]
- parser regex: ensure request_id and trace_id are captured as keywords for fast correlation.

Exception approval template (timeboxed exception):
- Exception ID: EXC-<YYYYMMDD>-<short>
- Requester: <name/email/team>
- Reason (short): <why elevated access is required now>
- Duration: <start ISO8601> to <end ISO8601> (max 48 hours unless PC approved)
- Compensating controls: <audit stream flagged, 1:1 monitoring, cron revocation>
- Evidence attached: RBAC-diff, audit-sample, siem-smoke, canary-snapshot
- Approvals required: SR (mandatory), RL (mandatory), OL (if impacts monitoring), PC (if required)

Signature block (copy into Jira comment or approval form):
- Release Lead: ____________________  Date: ________
- Security Reviewer: ________________  Date: ________
- Observability Lead: _______________  Date: ________
- SRE Oncall: ______________________  Date: ________

Post-approval automation (must run immediately after rollforward):
- Trigger `evidence-freeze`: snapshot current state and copy evidence to immutable bucket with checksum.
- Start extended audit collection for 72 hours (high-fidelity indexing).
- Schedule revocation job for any temporary artifacts at exception expiry time.
- Create retrospective ticket to review exception and include lessons learned.

Quick checklist for signoff (single-line entries for checklist UI):
- [ ] RBAC diff attached and least-privilege validated
- [ ] Audit sample contains required fields and representative events
- [ ] SIEM ingestion smoke test passed
- [ ] Canary gating criteria defined and dashboards linked
- [ ] Evidence automation ran and artifacts are in evidence bucket
- [ ] Revocation and containment plan documented
- [ ] RL, SR, OL, SRE signoffs obtained

Open questions / known limitations (notes for reviewers):
- Some legacy audit producers still emit non-ISO timestamps — cooperation with infra needed to normalize on ingestion.
- For on-prem/private deployments, evidence shipping may be manual if outbound connectivity restricted; ensure offline packaging instructions are followed.
- RBAC v2 rollout for some older tooling requires a compatibility shim; we accept shims only when covered by explicit testcases included in evidence pack (attach test run IDs).

References / handy commands:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/RBAC+v2+Design
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4821 (RBAC rollout epic)
- PR example for evidence automation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2983
- SIEM onboarding doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/SIEM+Onboarding

Notes to reviewers (quick):
This is a working draft focused on practical items reviewers will need during a pressured release window. Aim to automate the generation of the evidence pack so signoffs are based on verifiable artifacts rather than manual screenshots. If anything here is unclear, ping me (Aisha) in #sec-release with the release id.
